source.title: How do simple rotations affect the implicit bias of Adam?
source.authors: Adela DePavia; Vasileios Charisopoulos; Rebecca Willett

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests Adam and SignGD against GD on a synthetic classification task and finds that the adaptive methods’ relative generalization changes with data rotation; EGOP reparameterization restores their richer boundaries.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical decision-boundary results and finite-sample experiments. Figure descriptions provide qualitative outcomes, but no test-error values are stated. Results cited from Vasudeva et al. are not extracted as this paper’s results.
record.test_reason: The study examines optimizer-dependent generalization on a synthetic Gaussian-mixture task using full-batch GD, Adam and SignGD. V4 concerns held-out performance on image and language benchmarks under specified tuning regimes. These synthetic decision-boundary comparisons do not test that scoped version, and no results test V1–V3 or V5–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: Adam's richness bias depends on input representation, and small rotations can reverse its advantage over GD. The authors establish EGOP equivariance under their assumptions and empirically restore nonlinear boundaries using EGOP together with increased epsilon; EGOP alone is not demonstrated sufficient for that restoration.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic binary classification with two-layer ReLU networks and linear correlation loss; compares Adam and memoryless SignGD with GD under data rotations and EGOP reparameterization, rather than benchmark comparisons under limited tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: Data rotation changes the learned boundary; EGOP reparameterization restores equivariance; epsilon also changes the result, but larger epsilon alone does not restore nonlinear equivariant boundaries.

fits_no_version.finding: On the unrotated synthetic task, Adam and SignGD learn nonlinear boundaries closer to Bayes than GD; a small rotation produces linear boundaries with poorer generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On this synthetic binary-classification distribution, the relative generalization of Adam and SignGD versus full-batch GD depends on input orientation.

fits_no_version.finding: EGOP reparameterization together with epsilon 3.0 restores nonlinear, rotation-equivariant boundaries; increasing epsilon alone gives nearly linear boundaries and improves generalization for some rotations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On the tested synthetic task, reparameterization and epsilon jointly affect adaptive optimizers' decision boundaries and generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 reports that at rotation pi/4, Adam, SignGD and GD learn identical linear decision boundaries. Figure 4 retains the small-rotation failure when biases and outer-layer weights are trainable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The synthetic rotation effect depends on rotation angle and persists under some architectural relaxations.

record.problems: The evidence is a stylized synthetic binary classification task. The reported generalization comparisons are qualitative decision-boundary descriptions without test-error values or uncertainty estimates. Experiments use finite samples and full-batch gradients; theoretical results concern population loss and SignGD.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results identified. Related-work results attributed to prior studies were not extracted as this paper’s results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under matched architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Image and language benchmark performance under limited or broader tuning; SGD or momentum-SGD comparisons; decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching and word-level language models.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence and augmentation interactions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and competing measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: The paper explicitly discusses generalization, so the issue is the match to the scoped claim versions, rather than simply the absence of numerical test errors. Row states are cannot_determine relative to those versions; the reported synthetic boundary effects remain valid adjacent findings.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

No image-classification or language benchmark, broader optimizer tuning, AdamW/decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, or word-level language-model comparison. The paper tests Adam and SignGD versus GD on a synthetic binary classification task under data rotations and EGOP reparameterization.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.

rows.baseline: EGOP reparameterization with epsilon 3.0: nonlinear, equivariant boundaries
rows.value: Nearly linear boundary even at γ = 0; larger epsilon alone does not produce nonlinear, equivariant boundaries. At γ = π/32 the boundary is closer to GD and generalizes better than Adam with epsilon 10−8.
rows.note: The paper reports a relative improvement for the π/32 rotation but says larger epsilon alone does not produce the EGOP result.
rows.check: This epsilon ablation measures synthetic boundary behavior, outside V4's scope. It combines three rotation conditions and omits SignGD, which Figure 5 also evaluates. Correct the sample count to 10^4; '3/3' is not a reported outcome statistic.

reader_labels.reason: Adam and SignGD have nonlinear boundaries closer to Bayes than GD, contrary to the worse-adaptive-performance direction; see R1–R3.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Rotated synthetic classification, γ = π/32, without EGOP reparameterization
reader_labels.reason: Adam and SignGD learn the fixed linear boundary and generalize worse than GD and Bayes; see R4–R5.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The poorer relative result is not invariant to the training setup: EGOP reparameterization restores richer, equivariant boundaries, while larger epsilon alone yields only a partial improvement at γ = π/32; see R6–R8.
